# 2 Maccabees Chapter 7 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_007_page_001.jpg

---

**1** It happened also that seven brothers were arrested along with their mother, and the king tried to compel them by means of whips and scourges to eat unlawful pork.

**2** One of them, speaking for the rest, said: "What do you intend to ask of us and find out? We are ready to die rather than transgress the laws of our fathers."

**3** The king was infuriated and gave orders that pans and caldrons be heated.

**4** These were heated without delay. He commanded that the tongue of the spokesman be cut out, that he be scalped, and that his hands and feet be cut off, while the rest of the brothers and the mother looked on.

**5** When he was utterly incapacitated, the king ordered them to bring him still breathing to the fire and fry him in the pan. While the fumes from the pan spread everywhere, the brothers together with the mother encouraged one another to die nobly, saying:

**6** "The LORD God is watching, and he truly has compassion on us, as Moses declared in the song that bears witness against the people to their face, saying, 'And he will have compassion on his servants.'"

**7** When the first died in this way, they brought the second for their amusement. After tearing off the skin of his head along with the hair, they asked him: "Will you eat before your body is punished limb by limb?"

**8** He answered in the language of his ancestors and said to them: "Never." And so he in turn underwent the next stages of torture,

**9** and at his last breath he said: "You accursed wretch — you are releasing us from this present life, but the King of the universe will raise us up to an everlasting renewal of life, because we have died for his laws."

**10** After him, the third was subjected to their cruel sport. When commanded, he put out his tongue promptly and stretched out his hands courageously,

**11** and said with noble bearing: "These I received from Heaven, and for the sake of his laws I disdain them, and from him I hope to receive them back again."

**12** The king himself and those with him were struck with amazement at the spirit of the young man, for he made nothing of his sufferings.

**13** When he too had died, they tortured the fourth in the same way, treating him with similar cruelty.

**14** When he was near death, he said: "It is better to die at the hands of men and to cherish the hope that God himself will raise us up. But for you there will be no resurrection to life."

**15** Next they brought the fifth and maltreated him.

**16** Looking at the king, he said: "You have authority over human beings, mortal as you are, and you do what you please. But do not think that God has abandoned our people.

**17** Just wait, and you will see his great power — how he will torment you and your descendants."

**18** After him they brought the sixth. When he was about to die, he said: "Do not deceive yourself to no purpose. We are suffering these things on our own account, because we have sinned against our own God, and things worthy of astonishment have come upon us.

**19** But do not suppose that you will go unpunished for having dared to fight against God."

**20** The mother was especially admirable and worthy of honorable remembrance. Although she watched her seven sons perish in the space of a single day, she bore it with courage because of her hope in the LORD.

**21** She encouraged each of them in the language of their fathers, and being filled with a noble spirit she reinforced her womanly feeling with a man's courage and said to them:

**22** "I do not know how you came to be in my womb. It was not I who gave you life and breath, nor I who arranged the elements that make up each of you.

**23** Therefore the Creator of the world, who shaped the first formation of man and devised the origin of all things, will in his mercy give life and breath back to you again — since you now hold your own lives cheap for the sake of his laws."

**24** Antiochus felt that he was being treated with contempt, and he was suspicious of what sounded like a reproachful voice. Since the youngest was still alive, Antiochus not only appealed to him in words but even guaranteed with oaths that he would make him rich and prosperous if he would renounce his ancestral ways, and that he would take him as a Friend and entrust him with official responsibilities.

**25** Since the young man paid no attention to him at all, the king summoned the mother and urged her to advise the boy to save himself.

**26** After much urging on his part, she agreed to persuade her son.

**27** But leaning close to him, she spoke in her native tongue, mocking the cruel tyrant: "My son, have pity on me. I carried you nine months in my womb and nursed you for three years, and I have reared you and brought you to this point in your life and cared for you.

**28** I beg you, my child, to look at the heaven and the earth and see all that is in them, and to understand that God did not make them out of things that existed. And in the same way the human race came into being.

**29** Do not be afraid of this butcher, but prove worthy of your brothers. Accept death, so that by God's mercy I may receive you back along with your brothers."

**30** While she was still speaking, the young man said: "What are you waiting for? I will not obey the king's command, but I obey the command of the law that was given to our fathers through Moses.

**31** But you, who have devised every kind of evil against the Hebrews, will certainly not escape the hands of God.

**32** For we are suffering on account of our own sins.

**33** And if our living LORD is angry for a little while, for the purpose of rebuke and discipline, he will again be reconciled with his own servants.

**34** But you, unholy man, you most defiled of all people — do not be lifted up in vain and buoyed up by empty hopes when you raise your hand against the servants of God.

**35** You have not yet escaped the judgment of the almighty, all-seeing God.

**36** For our brothers, after enduring a brief suffering, have now drunk of ever-flowing life under God's covenant; but you, by God's judgment, will receive just penalty for your arrogance.

**37** I, like my brothers, surrender body and soul for the laws of our fathers. I call upon God to show favor quickly to our nation, and through trials and plagues to bring you to confess that he alone is God,

**38** and through me and my brothers to bring to an end the wrath of the Almighty that has justly fallen upon our whole nation."

**39** The king, enraged and inflamed by the young man's contemptuous tone, treated him more savagely than all the others.

**40** So he too died undefiled, trusting completely in the LORD.

**41** Last of all, after her sons, the mother died.

**42** Let this be sufficient concerning the eating of sacrificial food and the extreme tortures.
